business.description: DCM Nouvelle Limited is a manufacturer and exporter of 100% cotton yarn, operating a spinning facility at Hisar, Haryana with 1,57,872 spindles. The company emerged from the demerger of DCM Limited and offers combed, carded, compact, and double yarns under brands FUTURO, PRIMERO, DINERO, and CCY, along with BCI and sustainable yarns, exporting to 16 countries.

outlook.statement: India's emergence as a preferred global sourcing destination, supported by its strong manufacturing capabilities, skilled workforce, and growing demand for sustainable, high-quality textile products, presents significant opportunities. The Company remains optimistic about the long-term prospects of the Indian textile sector and confident in its ability to leverage these opportunities through customer-centric approach, operational excellence, and strategic investments.

Strategic priorities remain focused on: Enhancing operational efficiencies and manufacturing excellence; Strengthening and diversifying product portfolio; Expanding presence across global markets; Accelerating innovation and customer-centric product development; Increasing focus on value-added and specialty products; Leveraging manufacturing capabilities to drive profitable and sustainable growth.

Optimistic about long-term prospects of specialty chemicals sector; focused on developing new innovative value-added specialty amine products, enhancing operational efficiency through technology and process optimization, strengthening quality/safety/environmental stewardship, expanding customer relationships in domestic and international markets, investing in research for new product development and sustainable manufacturing practices.

Focused on enhancing operational competitiveness through process optimization, technology adoption, cost rationalization; accelerating value creation through diversification via specialty chemicals subsidiary; expanding global reach and customer partnerships; digital and technology-led transformation; sustainability as competitive advantage; investing in human capital; strengthening financial resilience.
India cotton yarn market projected to grow from 10.92 USD Billion in 2025 to 22.5 USD Billion by 2035, exhibiting a CAGR of 7.4% during 2025-2035.
Ministry of Textiles Vision 2030 objective of expanding textile exports from current ~₹3 lakh crore to about ₹9 lakh crore through stronger domestic manufacturing and wider global outreach.
Global amines market approx. USD 20-25 billion, expected to grow at ~6-7% from 2024 to 2030.
Indian aliphatic and aromatic amines market on dynamic growth path supported by strong demand from pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and industrial applications.

Export potential for Indian-manufactured aliphatic and aromatic amines substantial, particularly in European and US markets, driven by rising demand for green chemistry, technological advancements, and economic growth.

The Company remains well-positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities and create sustainable value for all stakeholders while reinforcing its vision of being a preferred global supplier of high-quality cotton yarn.

DCM Nouvelle Specialty Chemicals Limited continues to focus on enhancing capacity utilization, improving operational efficiencies and expanding its customer base to achieve sustainable profitability in the coming years.

AMPIN C&I Power Three Private Limited continues to focus on the execution and timely commissioning of its project, which is expected to facilitate the commencement of commercial operations and revenue generation in the subsequent periods.

Chemicals CGU revenue projections based on management's approved business plan incorporating ramp-up of existing manufacturing operations and market penetration for specialty chemicals; projections include only operating and recurring revenues from domestic sales aligned with capacity utilisation expected to scale progressively to full plant capacity by FY2029; no revenue from export operations or uncommitted future projects included.

EBITDA margins projected to improve progressively from approximately 12% to 22% over explicit forecast period (FY2027 to FY2031) driven by operating leverage from volume scale-up, stabilisation of fixed overheads, optimised product mix, and normalisation of start-up inefficiencies.
Capital expenditure assumptions include approved expansionary capex in FY2027 (Phase-II expansion); no further material capex assumed from FY2028 to FY2031.
